title: Why an ice cream machine heats its own mix
script: This ice cream machine deliberately heats its own mix. So what happens when you ask for a cone? Inside the Taylor C602 used at McDonald's, the mix sits in a hopper and a freezing barrel. Every day, a heat-treatment cycle takes it to about sixty-six Celsius, holds it hot, then cools it down. The cooling stage gets two hours. Let's follow one imaginary night. Heating goes through. Cooling takes too long. The controller soft-locks the machine, and your cone has to wait. To find out what happened, you can look back through the cycle record. There's the failed stage, how long it took, and temperatures saved every five minutes. Here, the mix was still too warm when time ran out. That gives the person fixing it somewhere to start. Once the problem's sorted, the machine needs a successful heat cycle or the required cleaning before serving again. Plenty of other things can stop a machine. This is one of them.
